parallel.requirements: The parallel parent and workflow recognized the core requirements: pure ESM Node, hierarchical modules, no external dependencies, no Python, no crypto module, exact JWT and argparse behavior, and /output/test1.mjs.
parallel.plan_and_ownership: The workflow assigned four parallel Spec probes first, then one Build implementation agent, then planned Verify, Fix, and Final phases. Implementation ownership existed, but it was sequenced after all investigation.
parallel.implementation: The build agent started late and wrote only library modules such as utf8, base64url, sha256, hmac, python-json, jose, errors, and stdio helpers.
parallel.integration_and_delivery: The delivered artifact lacked the required /output/test1.mjs entry point and lacked the planned argparse module, so the final artifact was not executable as requested.
parallel.verification: The workflow prompt required a self-test, and the parent attempted a smoke test, but the run was killed before a Node entry existed or any integrated verification completed.
parallel.unfinished_or_incorrect: The official artifact validation rejected the output because test1.mjs was missing, and the current official evaluation passed 0 of 70 samples.

serial.requirements: The serial actor recognized the same ESM, no-dependency, no-Python, no-crypto, hierarchical-module, exact CLI, and JWT behavior requirements.
serial.plan_and_ownership: The serial actor kept probing, implementation, integration, and verification in one local control loop with no delegation or subagents.
serial.implementation: The serial run wrote bytes, SHA-256, HMAC, base64url, pyjson, argparse, formatting, JOSE, JWT, process-argv modules, and the required /output/test1.mjs entry.
serial.integration_and_delivery: The output tree contained test1.mjs and coherent support modules, and artifact validation accepted the expected entry file.
serial.verification: The serial actor matched four samples, fixed differential mismatches, reran a 98-case suite to pass=98 fail=0, ran byte-exact terminal-width checks, and generated a larger fuzz corpus before timeout.
serial.unfinished_or_incorrect: Despite its better coverage and accepted entry file, the official evaluator still marked solution_passed false with 51 of 70 samples passed.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: Parallel recognized the required /output/test1.mjs, ESM modules, no dependency, no Python, no crypto, argparse, JSON, and JWT obligations.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: Serial recognized the same obligations directly from the prompt and probes.
comparison_dimensions.difference: There was no meaningful requirement-recognition gap; the difference was that serial carried the requirements into a delivered entry file while parallel did not reach delivery.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: Parallel decomposed into four Spec probes first and one later Build owner, with planned Verify, Fix, and Final phases after that.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: Serial used one actor for probing, writing, correcting, and verification without delegation.
comparison_dimensions.difference: Parallel's useful implementation owner existed but started only after the probe phase; serial kept implementation on the critical path from the beginning.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: The Build prompt included the task context, spec digest, required module layout, entry path, and self-test requirement.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: The serial actor held requirements and implementation context in one thread while probing and writing the modules.
comparison_dimensions.difference: The evidence does not support a missing brief or missing interface contract; context was present, but the implementation phase was delayed.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: Parallel wrote several support modules but did not write the executable entry point or complete the CLI parsing layer.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: Serial wrote the support modules and the required /output/test1.mjs entry point.
comparison_dimensions.difference: Serial completed an executable integrated path; parallel stopped at partial libraries.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: The delegated implementation was still active when interrupted, and the parent never received a completed build result.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: The serial actor's writes remained directly in the output tree and did not require a child result join.
comparison_dimensions.difference: Parallel had no complete delegated implementation to join; serial's final tree was already assembled in place.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: Parallel probe agents used scratch work and one build agent wrote final modules; no concrete write collision was observed, but the final tree was incomplete.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: Serial used one writer and produced a coherent tree that artifact validation accepted.
comparison_dimensions.difference: The shared-state difference is completeness, not collision: serial's tree included the entry point while parallel's final tree did not.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: Parallel required self-testing in the build prompt, but the parent smoke-test attempt ended with exit code 137 and official evaluation passed 0 of 70.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: Serial ran samples, a differential suite, byte-exact terminal-width checks, and generated fuzz cases before official evaluation passed 51 of 70.
comparison_dimensions.difference: Serial obtained real whole-program verification on an existing entry file; parallel reached neither entry-file execution nor integrated verification.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: Parallel spent the first phase on all probes, including stalled retries, and entered Build late enough that only partial modules existed at shutdown.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: Serial also timed out but had already written and tested a runnable artifact.
comparison_dimensions.difference: Parallel closure pressure landed before delivery; serial closure pressure landed after delivery and verification, explaining the large quality gap without a pass/fail discordance.

outcome_analysis.explanation: Both runs failed officially, so no retained pattern is claimed to explain a discordant outcome. The materially different result is quality and delivery: parallel artifact validation failed because test1.mjs was absent and the evaluator passed 0 of 70, while serial delivered test1.mjs, validated the artifact, and passed 51 of 70.
parallel_contributors: The parallel workflow deferred implementation until all Spec probes and retries completed, leaving the Build phase with insufficient time.
The build child was interrupted after writing support libraries but before /output/test1.mjs and before required integrated self-testing.
serial_contributors: The serial actor wrote /output/test1.mjs and support modules directly.
The serial actor ran sample, differential, byte-exact, and fuzz-oriented verification before timeout.
ordinary_implementation_differences: The serial implementation still failed 19 official samples, so ordinary remaining semantic defects existed outside the retained concurrency pattern.
The parallel implementation was incomplete at the artifact level and therefore could not exercise the task behavior.
outcome_analysis.causal_scope: no pass-fail outcome difference; supported comparative explanation for the artifact-quality gap

candidates.reason: The workflow explicitly assigned a build:implementation child to write the implementation under /output; the issue was late/incomplete execution, not absent ownership.
There were not separately owned component implementations requiring an unowned reconciler; one build child owned the integrated module tree.
The build child was explicitly told to create /output/test1.mjs and the module spine; missing delivery reflects incomplete late execution, not an unassigned assembly step.
The workflow script defined Spec, Build, Verify, Fix, and Final phases under a single orchestrator, so the end-to-end pipeline had an owner even though it did not complete.
The qualifying gate was not one mandatory serial preflight; the workflow launched multiple investigators concurrently and waited for that separate investigation phase before building.
Four investigative probes overlapped with each other, but productive implementation was deferred until after the Spec phase completed and retries consumed the available window.
candidates.realized_consequence: The build phase was deadline-constrained and interrupted with only partial libraries, no /output/test1.mjs, no argparse module, and no completed integrated verification.
candidates.near_match_reason: Multiple investigators ran concurrently; the harmful boundary was the separate all-investigation-first phase, not a single required preflight gate.

candidates.reason: The implementation path did start too late, but that is captured more specifically by Serial Investigation for the same episode and consequence.
The probe breadth and retries consumed budget, but the direct harmful boundary was the all-probes-before-build sequencing, so a separate fan-out label would double count the same chain.
The build assignment was broad, but the evidence does not isolate overbroad child scope as distinct from the late start created by the prior investigation phase.

The build child brief included the task context, required module layout, exact /output/test1.mjs entry path, and required self-test; the child did not fail because a known requirement was omitted from the brief.
The probes produced findings for one build owner rather than separate owned components expected to interoperate, and no incompatible independently produced component interface was observed.
No specific known requirement or current-file fact is shown disappearing through transfer and causing repeated work or wrong action.
The spec digest was large, but the build child consumed it enough to begin writing modules; no evidence shows decision-structure overload as the cause of unfinished delivery.
No child or parent consumed a superseded workspace or requirement state; the issue was late implementation after the spec phase.
Although probe findings included tension about invalid UTF-8 handling, the build child explicitly adjudicated it before writing, so no unadjudicated conflict caused integration failure.
The parent and workflow did not present the whole task as complete; the run was killed before an accepted integrated artifact or completion decision.
The observed retries were stalled probe retries with new completed findings, not replacement implementation attempts that repeated prior work without checkpoint state.

taxonomy_decisions.sub_label: Wrong Start, Join, or Result Timing

candidates.reason: The build child was interrupted by run shutdown, but this is the downstream terminal state of the same late-build chain, not a distinct parent stop decision with a separate corrective boundary.
No complete directly promotable candidate or compatible component set existed; partial libraries without test1.mjs do not qualify for late finalization.
No child result was merged after integrated verification, and the parallel run did not reach the planned verification phase.
The delegated implementation was not completed or retrievable as a usable candidate, so there was no completed implementation result for the parent to join.
The workflow never reached a verifier child producing a concrete finding; there was no verifier result trapped below the parent.
The child did not fail early with an observable parent decision point for takeover; the run ended as the same timeout/interruption chain already covered by Serial Investigation.
The parent used or observed completed probe status and no completed implementation result was available and ignored.
The parent repeatedly inspected /output and the workflow journal while waiting; the wait was not blind even though it ended in timeout.
No concurrent agents wrote competing implementation paths or overlapping final responsibilities; probes avoided /output and one build child wrote final files.
No two live agents edited the same source or configuration file and no reconciliation of same-file edits was observed.
No agent replaced, deleted, recreated, or wholesale rewrote non-entry source produced by another agent.
The required deliverable test1.mjs was never produced, so there was no executable entry-point overwrite.
No broad cleanup, rebuild, or promotion replaced multiple existing final outputs or invalidated another agent's final-tree work.
The probes were instructed not to write under /output and the final workspace was written by one build child, with no concrete unstable-state or provenance problem from simultaneous writers.
No generated file, cache, fixture, tool, or temporary artifact from one concurrent actor was consumed by another as stable reference input.

retained_patterns.reason: Parallel used concurrent probe agents, but treated investigation as a separate first phase and deferred productive implementation until those probes and retries completed. The late build then stopped before the required entry file and verification.
retained_patterns.realized_consequence: Build remained incomplete at shutdown, leaving only support libraries in the artifact, no /output/test1.mjs, and no completed integrated verification.
retained_patterns.near_match_reason: The workflow did not wait on one serial oracle; it waited for a whole parallel investigation phase before starting implementation.

suppressed_same_chain_candidates: Critical-Path Starvation, Fan-out Budget Exhaustion, Oversized Child Task, Early Child Termination, No Failure Takeover, and Blind Timeout Wait were screened but rejected as downstream descriptions of the same delayed-build and timeout chain.

cardinality_audit.overlabel_check: No additional label was retained for missing owner, context transfer, result lifecycle, monitoring, write collision, or contamination because each lacked a distinct episode, consequence, and corrective boundary.
